item.title: A measurement-free quantum error correction protocol for superconducting cavities
item.description:
Pay dirt new method — Simulated measurement-free QEC using a three-cavity binomial code corrects single-photon loss with 99% fidelity and achieves logical lifetime gain of G=1.20 to 1.84 over the unprotected Fock encoding.

Grade 0.493 · 2.2σ above the day's baseline · matched “Superconducting Qubits: Current State of Play” · Q. Rumman Rahman, S. M. Girvin, D. K. Weiss

Figure

QEC gain G(τ) as a function of inter-cycle waiting time τ/T1cav for T1cav=0.5,1,2ms, peaking above 1.0 (break-even) across all tested cavity lifetimes, and single-round infidelity error budgets.

Asks

Can a measurement-free error-correction protocol for photonic modes be adapted to a three-cavity circuit QED platform to surpass break-even without syndrome measurement or feed-forward?

Before

Six-mode photonic architecture using the Chuang-Leung-Yamamoto code (Krastanov et al. 2021); here reduced to three cavities via the lowest-order binomial code.

But

Numerical simulations with sub-5 µs gate sequence; transmon coherence fixed at T1tr=T2tr=300μs; cavity lifetimes between 0.5ms and 2ms.

Tools

three superconducting microwave cavities · Josephson-junction nonlinear couplers · auxiliary transmons · GRAPE pulse optimization

Abstract

The realization of large-scale quantum computation will require quantum error correction (QEC). One way to reduce the demands placed on QEC is to correct dominant physical errors at a lower level before passing the remaining errors to an outer code. Recently, Krastanov et al. [Nat. Commun. 12, 191 (2021)] proposed a measurement-free error-correction protocol based on coherent control of photonic modes that corrects for photon loss. Here, we adapt this approach to a circuit quantum electrodynamics (cQED) architecture using three superconducting microwave cavities coupled by Josephson-junction-based nonlinear elements. We encode the logical qubit in the lowest-order binomial code of one cavity, while the two other cavities serve as ancillas. Using numerical simulations with experimentally realistic parameters, we demonstrate that our protocol can correct single-photon loss with 99% fidelity. Furthermore, we optimize the waiting time between successive rounds of error-correction, and show that the logical lifetime can be extended by a factor of 1.2-1.8 relative to the unprotected Fock |0⟩, |1⟩ encoding, surpassing break-even performance. Our work highlights the potential of gate-based, measurement-free QEC for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

item.title: Parallel transversal entangling gates for fault-tolerant trapped-ion quantum computing
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Parallel transversal controlled-Z gate across neighboring trapped-ion double wells engineers desired pairwise couplings using dynamical decoupling and geometric cancellation, requiring 𝒪(n) time intervals and 𝒪(n2) single-qubit pulses while achieving shorter gate duration and lower two-photon Rabi frequency than sequential pair gates.

Grade 0.451 · 1.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “transmon and fluxonium coherence, single- and two-qubit gate fidelity” · Katrin Bolsmann, Alan Kahan, Alejandro Bermúdez, Markus Müller

Figure

Logical Bell-state infidelity between two [[4,1,2]] code blocks as a function of physical CZ gate error rate for various laser wave-vector misalignments ϵ. Quadratic error suppression transitions to a crosstalk-induced error floor proportional to ϵ2 at small physical error rates.

Asks

How can transversal entangling gates between trapped-ion registers in separate trapping wells be executed natively in parallel without being degraded by all-to-all phonon-mediated couplings?

But

Assumes instantaneous, perfect decoupling π-pulses, no motional heating, and suppressed AC Stark shifts; wave-vector misalignment ϵ induces residual ZZ crosstalk setting an error floor pfloor≈π2δ2ϵ2/(ωCOM+ωSTR)2.

Tools

quantum spring array architecture · dynamical decoupling (Walsh-Hadamard sequences) · geometric cancellation via wave-vector alignment · effective Ising Hamiltonian simulation

Abstract

Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires high-fidelity entangling gates that can be implemented efficiently across multiple qubit pairs. We present a scheme for simultaneous pairwise entangling operations, i.e., a transversal controlled-Z gate, across neighboring wells in a double-well trapped-ion architecture. A tailored dynamical decoupling scheme suppresses unwanted couplings with a pulse count that scales quadratically with the number of ions. We show that incorporating a genuine geometric cancellation reduces the pulse count and, for selected register sizes, allows the parallel operation to be completed faster than an equivalent sequence of two-qubit gates while requiring a significantly smaller two-photon Rabi frequency. We assess the experimental feasibility of the protocol by analyzing the impact of decoherence and crosstalk arising from laser wave-vector misalignment. To gain insight into the robustness of fault-tolerant protocols against realistic imperfections of the proposed transversal gate scheme, we investigate how crosstalk-induced gate errors affect the fault-tolerant preparation of a logical Bell state between two [[4,1,2]] quantum-error-detection code blocks. These results highlight the potential of transversal entangling gates as a building block for trapped-ion-based scalable fault-tolerant quantum error correction.

item.title: High-fidelity control of long-lived data qubits via a noisy mediator
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Dividing gates into M short segments interleaved with mediator reinitialization suppresses mediator-decoherence error variance by 1/M2, achieving gate fidelities approaching 99.99% even when two-qubit gate duration exceeds mediator coherence time.

Grade 0.444 · 1.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “Semiconductor spin qubits” · Nguyen H. Le, Tikai Chang, Eran Ginossar, Michael Stern

Figure

Gate infidelity plotted against segment count M for single-qubit and two-qubit rotations. Shows mediator-induced infidelity declining as M increases, matching analytical scaling down to the 10−4 level.

Asks

Can high-fidelity quantum gates be executed on long-lived data qubits via a lossy mediator without quantum error correction or heralded postselection?

Before

Path-independent gates and error-transparent schemes relied on heralded postselection or quantum-error-correcting codes, while uncorrected gates were bounded by mediator coherence time.

But

Neglects data-qubit decoherence during gates; assumes segment duration τ and reset error ζ are small enough to neglect multiple quantum jumps per segment; requires fast mediator reset relative to gate time.

Tools

quantum-trajectory analysis · segmented reinitialization / reset-assisted control · effective cross-resonance / multi-body Hamiltonian engineering · quantum master-equation simulations

Abstract

Long-lived qubits are attractive for storing quantum information, but they are often difficult to control or couple directly. A common strategy is to use mediator qubits to generate effective interactions for gate implementation. However, the mediator typically has a shorter coherence time than the data qubits, so mediator relaxation and dephasing are expected to limit the achievable gate fidelity. Here, we show that this limitation can be overcome. We present a reset-assisted control method that suppresses mediator-induced errors and enables high-fidelity single- and two-qubit gates on a quantum register of long-lived data qubits. Although mediator quantum jumps render the data-qubit evolution stochastic, repeated mediator reinitialization drives the resulting evolution paths toward the desired target operation. An analytical quantum-trajectory analysis reveals the physical mechanism of error suppression and provides compact fidelity formulas for adapting the method to different platforms. Our results relax the requirement for long mediator coherence, broadening the range of mediators that can support high-fidelity control.
